explain.say: Scars slowly remodel and fade over a year or more, but they never quite match normal skin. Even when mature, a scar has only about 80 percent of the strength of the original skin.

marks.label: About 80% at best
marks.ask: Is a scar as strong as normal skin?

faq.q: What is a scar made of?
faq.a: A scar is made mostly of collagen, the same protein that gives normal skin its strength, but laid down quickly in straight, tightly packed bundles instead of a woven pattern.

faq.q: What makes normal skin stretchy and strong?
faq.a: The dermis contains collagen fibres woven in many directions plus elastic fibres called elastin. This basket-like weave lets skin stretch and spring back.

faq.q: Is a scar as strong as normal skin?
faq.a: No. A fully healed scar reaches at most about 80 percent of the strength of the original skin, because its collagen is not woven as well.
Hair follicles and sweat glands are complex structures that the body does not rebuild in deep wounds. The scar patch is plain collagen, so hair does not grow there.

faq.q: Why do some cuts heal without a scar?
faq.a: If only the top layer of skin, the epidermis, is damaged, it regrows perfectly from the cells below. Scars form when the wound reaches the deeper dermis.

facts: A mature scar reaches at most about 80 percent of the strength of uninjured skin.
Scar remodelling can continue for a year or more after a wound heals.
